ucs.title: [LLM] Midnight Blizzard (APT29/SVR) cloud password-spray fan-out from residential proxy → OAuth/service-principal credential add
ucs.description: Hunts the exact SVR cloud-intrusion chain Microsoft documented in the Jan 2024 Midnight Blizzard incident: low-and-slow password spraying via residential-proxy / legacy-auth against a fan-out of accounts, immediately followed by addition of credentials or secrets to an OAuth application / service principal for persistent token-based access. Tied to APT29 because the spray→app-credential-abuse combination (T1110.003 → T1098.001/T1528) is their signature cloud TTP, not generic brute force.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats summariesonly=true allow_old_summaries=true count, dc(Authentication.user) as distinct_users, values(Authentication.user) as users from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=failure AND Authentication.app IN ("AzureActiveDirectory","office365","Entra") by Authentication.src Authentication.signature _time span=1h
| `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")`
| where distinct_users >= 10
| join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=true count as success_count, values(Authentication.user) as success_users from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=success AND Authentication.app IN ("AzureActiveDirectory","office365","Entra") by Authentication.src | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")`]
| table _time, src, signature, distinct_users, users, success_count, success_users
| sort - distinct_users
ucs.kql:
// APT29 / Midnight Blizzard cloud password-spray fan-out
let SprayWindow = 1h;
let Sprays = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ErrorCode == 50126        // 50126 = invalid username or password (spray signal)
    | where IPAddress != ""
    | summarize FailedUsers = dcount(AccountUpn),
                Attempts = count(),
                SampleUsers = make_set(AccountUpn, 50),
                LegacyAuth = make_set(ClientAppUsed, 10)
                by IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, SprayWindow)
    | where FailedUsers >= 10;        // 10 = fan-out across distinct accounts in 1h (P99 of legit typo bursts ~4)
let SuccessfulFromSprayIP = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | project SuccessTime = Timestamp, IPAddress, CompromisedUpn = AccountUpn, ClientAppUsed, UserAgent, Country;
Sprays
| join kind=inner SuccessfulFromSprayIP on IPAddress
| where SuccessTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 6h)   // success shortly after the spray from same egress IP
| project SprayHour = Timestamp, IPAddress, FailedUsers, Attempts, SampleUsers, LegacyAuth,
          SuccessTime, CompromisedUpn, ClientAppUsed, UserAgent, Country
| order by FailedUsers desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// APT29 / Midnight Blizzard spray fan-out → followed by app/SP credential add (AuditLogs)
let SprayWindow = 1h;
let Sprays = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ResultType == 50126        // invalid username or password
    | where isnotempty(IPAddress)
    | summarize FailedUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
                Attempts = count(),
                SampleUsers = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 50),
                LegacyAuth = make_set(ClientAppUsed, 10)
                by IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, SprayWindow)
    | where FailedUsers >= 10;
let CredAdds = AuditLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where OperationName in ("Add service principal credentials", "Update application – Certificates and secrets management", "Add application credentials", "Consent to application")
    | extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), ActorIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
    | project CredAddTime = TimeGenerated, OperationName, Actor, ActorIP, TargetResources;
Sprays
| join kind=inner CredAdds on $left.IPAddress == $right.ActorIP
| where CredAddTime between (TimeGenerated .. TimeGenerated + 24h)
| project SprayHour = TimeGenerated, IPAddress, FailedUsers, Attempts, SampleUsers, LegacyAuth,
          CredAddTime, OperationName, Actor, TargetResources
| order by FailedUsers desc
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog
| Status=/fail/i OR AuthenticationResult=/fail/i
| groupBy([SourceEndpointIpAddress], function=[count(field=UserPrincipal, distinct=true, as=DistinctUsers), count(as=Attempts), collect([UserPrincipal])])
| DistinctUsers >= 10
ucs.rationale: Generic brute-force fires on any single-account hammering. This requires the APT29-specific shape: distinct-account fan-out (spray, not brute) from one egress IP + a successful logon from that same residential-proxy IP, and on Sentinel correlates straight into the OAuth/service-principal credential-add that Midnight Blizzard used for persistence in the 2024 Microsoft/HPE intrusions. ucs.title: [LLM] APT29 EnvyScout/ROOTSAW ISO-LNK delivery → rundll32/regsvr32 DLL exec from mounted volume
ucs.description: Hunts APT29's spear-phishing-to-execution chain where an HTML-smuggled .iso/.img attachment is mounted and a LNK inside it launches rundll32.exe/regsvr32.exe against a bundled DLL on the non-C: mounted drive. Tied to APT29 (The Dukes/Cozy Bear) because the container-file → explorer double-click → signed-LOLBin-loads-DLL pattern (EnvyScout/ROOTSAW/BEATDROP loaders) is their characteristic delivery tradecraft used against diplomatic and government targets.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats summariesonly=true count, values(Processes.process) as cmdline, values(Processes.process_path) as process_path, min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","verclsid.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")`
| regex cmdline="(?i)\b[D-Z]:\\\\"
| regex cmdline="(?i)\.(dll|cpl|tmp|dat),?\s"
| convert ctime(firstTime)
| table firstTime, dest, user, parent_process_name, process_name, cmdline, process_path
| sort - firstTime
ucs.kql:
// APT29 EnvyScout ISO/IMG → LNK → rundll32/regsvr32 loading DLL off a mounted (non-C:) volume
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("rundll32.exe", "regsvr32.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe", "verclsid.exe")   // double-click of LNK inside mounted container
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b[D-Z]:\\"            // DLL referenced on a mounted drive, not C:
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".dll", ".cpl", ".tmp", ".dat", ".db", ".png")  // APT29 masquerades loader ext
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// APT29 EnvyScout ISO/IMG → LNK → rundll32/regsvr32 loading DLL off a mounted volume (4688)
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\regsvr32.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\verclsid.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b[D-Z]:\\"
| where CommandLine has_any (".dll", ".cpl", ".tmp", ".dat", ".db", ".png")
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT29 EnvyScout ISO-LNK rundll32/regsvr32 DLL execution from mounted volume
id: 8c1d6a7e-4b2f-4f9a-9d3a-2e7c1b9f0a44
status: experimental
description: Detects rundll32/regsvr32 launched by explorer (LNK double-click) loading a DLL off a non-C mounted drive, matching APT29 EnvyScout/ROOTSAW ISO delivery.
references:
  - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/tracking-apt29-phishing-campaigns
author: SOC Detection Engineering
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1218
  - attack.g0016
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\verclsid.exe'
  selection_drive:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\b[D-Z]:\\'
  selection_ext:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.dll'
      - '.cpl'
      - '.tmp'
      - '.dat'
      - '.db'
      - '.png'
  condition: selection_img and selection_parent and selection_drive and selection_ext
falsepositives:
  - Software installers run from genuine optical media or mounted ISOs
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\explorer.exe OR *\Explorer.exe OR *\verclsid.exe OR *\VerClsid.exe) @Image:(*\rundll32.exe OR *\RunDll32.exe OR *\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\RegSvr32.exe OR *\REGSVR32.EXE) @CommandLine:(*.dll* OR *.cpl* OR *.tmp* OR *.dat*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(explorer|verclsid)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(rundll32|regsvr32)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)\\b[D-Z]:\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)\\.(dll|cpl|tmp|dat|db|png),?", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=[count(as=cnt), collect([CommandLine])])
ucs.rationale: A bare rundll32/regsvr32 alert is noise. This pins the three discriminators of APT29's EnvyScout/ROOTSAW chain: explorer.exe (or verclsid) as parent (user double-clicked a LNK inside a mounted container, not a script/Office macro), the DLL referenced on a non-C: drive letter (the mounted .iso/.img APT29 ships to defeat MOTW), and the loader masquerade extensions APT29 favours.
